stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $AEC$?
stimulus: A geologist maps two fault traces as parallel lines $\ell$ and $m$, with $\ell$ above $m$. Points $F$, $A$, and $B$ lie on $\ell$ in that order from left to right. Points $C$ and $D$ lie on $m$, with $C$ to the left of $D$. Two seismic survey lines, segment $AD$ and segment $BC$, cross at point $E$ between the fault traces. The measure of angle $FAD$ is $142^\circ$, and the measure of angle $BCD$ is $75^\circ$.
explanation: Mark the figure as you go. Angles $FAD$ and $BAD$ form a linear pair on $\ell$, so $\angle BAD = 180^\circ - 142^\circ = 38^\circ$. Because $\ell \parallel m$, angles $ABC$ and $BCD$ are alternate interior angles cut by transversal $BC$, so $\angle ABC = 75^\circ$. In triangle $ABE$, $\angle AEB = 180^\circ - 38^\circ - 75^\circ = 67^\circ$. Angle $AEC$ forms a linear pair with angle $AEB$ along segment $BC$, so $\angle AEC = 180^\circ - 67^\circ = 113^\circ$. As a check, $AEC$ is an exterior angle of triangle $ABE$, so it also equals $38^\circ + 75^\circ$.

common_errors.why: Found the interior angle $AEB$ of triangle $ABE$ and stopped, without taking its supplement to get angle $AEC$.
Treated angles $ABC$ and $BCD$ as co-interior instead of alternate, so used $\angle ABC = 105^\circ$. That gives $\angle AEB = 37^\circ$ and $\angle AEC = 143^\circ$.
Found $\angle BAD = 38^\circ$ from the linear pair and gave that as the answer.

stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $ADC$?
stimulus: In a diagram of telescope sightlines, points $A$, $B$, and $C$ lie on a straight line, with $B$ between $A$ and $C$. Point $D$ is not on line $AC$. In the diagram, $AB = BD$ and $BD = DC$. The measure of angle $DAB$ is $28^\circ$.
explanation: Since $AB = BD$, triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with base $AD$, so $\angle BDA = \angle DAB = 28^\circ$. Angle $DBC$ is an exterior angle of triangle $ABD$, so $\angle DBC = 28^\circ + 28^\circ = 56^\circ$. Since $BD = DC$, triangle $BDC$ is isosceles with base $BC$, so $\angle DCB = \angle DBC = 56^\circ$, and $\angle BDC = 180^\circ - 56^\circ - 56^\circ = 68^\circ$. Angle $ADC$ is made up of angles $ADB$ and $BDC$, so $\angle ADC = 28^\circ + 68^\circ = 96^\circ$. As a check, in triangle $ADC$: $28^\circ + 96^\circ + 56^\circ = 180^\circ$.

common_errors.why: Found angle $BDC$ in the second triangle and stopped, forgetting to add angle $ADB$.
Treated $BD = BC$ instead of $BD = DC$, which puts the equal angles at $D$ and $C$. That gives $\angle BDC = (180^\circ - 56^\circ)/2 = 62^\circ$ and $\angle ADC = 28^\circ + 62^\circ = 90^\circ$.
Gave the exterior angle $DBC$, or the equal angle $DCB$, instead of angle $ADC$.
Gave angle $ABD$ ($180^\circ - 28^\circ - 28^\circ$), the vertex angle of the first triangle.

stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $ACB$?
stimulus: The excavated foundation of an ancient storehouse is the quadrilateral $ABCD$, with side $AB$ parallel to side $DC$. A wall runs along diagonal $AC$. In the plan, $AD = DC$, the measure of angle $ADC$ is $76^\circ$, and the measure of angle $ABC$ is $70^\circ$.
explanation: Since $AD = DC$, triangle $ADC$ is isosceles with base $AC$, so $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = (180^\circ - 76^\circ)/2 = 52^\circ$. Because $AB \parallel DC$ and $AC$ is a transversal, angle $CAB$ and angle $ACD$ are alternate interior angles, so $\angle CAB = 52^\circ$. In triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB = 180^\circ - 52^\circ - 70^\circ = 58^\circ$. As a check, angles $ABC$ and $BCD$ are co-interior, so $\angle BCD = 110^\circ$, and $110^\circ - 52^\circ = 58^\circ$.

common_errors.why: Found the base angle $ACD$ of the isosceles triangle and gave that instead of angle $ACB$.
Gave the whole angle $BCD$, found from co-interior angles, instead of only the part between $AC$ and $CB$.
Took the equal sides as meeting at $A$ instead of $D$, so set $\angle DCA = 76^\circ$. Then $\angle ACB = 110^\circ - 76^\circ = 34^\circ$.

stem: What is the measure, in degrees, of angle $EAP$?
stimulus: A printmaker carves two parallel grooves, lines $\ell$ and $m$, into a woodblock, with $\ell$ above $m$. Points $E$, $A$, and $C$ lie on $\ell$ in that order from left to right. Points $B$ and $D$ lie on $m$, with $B$ to the left of $D$. A bent cut runs from $A$ to point $P$ and then from $P$ to $B$. Point $P$ lies between the grooves and to the right of line $AB$. The measure of angle $CAP$ is $(3x)^\circ$, the measure of angle $DBP$ is $(2x + 5)^\circ$, and the measure of angle $APB$ is $(7x - 20)^\circ$. Angle $APB$ is the angle less than $180^\circ$.
explanation: Draw a line through $P$ parallel to $\ell$ and $m$. This splits angle $APB$ into two parts. The part next to $PA$ is an alternate interior angle with angle $CAP$, and the part next to $PB$ is an alternate interior angle with angle $DBP$. So $\angle APB = \angle CAP + \angle DBP$: $7x - 20 = 3x + (2x + 5)$, so $2x = 25$ and $x = 12.5$. Then $\angle CAP = 3(12.5) = 37.5^\circ$. Angles $EAP$ and $CAP$ form a linear pair on $\ell$, so $\angle EAP = 180^\circ - 37.5^\circ = 142.5^\circ$.

common_errors.why: Found angle $CAP$ and stopped, without taking its supplement to get angle $EAP$.
Solved for $x$ and gave it as the angle measure.
Took the supplement of the angle at $B$ ($180^\circ - 30^\circ$) instead of the supplement of the angle at $A$.
Treated $A$, $P$, and $B$ as a triangle and set $3x + (2x + 5) + (7x - 20) = 180$. That gives $x = 16.25$, so $\angle CAP = 48.75^\circ$ and $\angle EAP = 131.25^\circ$.
